purpose: Compare oracle ROI-384 with the frozen layer-5 L2+anchor selector at the same per-sample final visual-token budget on the revealed 192-image development split.
evidence_level: revealed development comparison; calibration and test splits remain sealed

model.decode: custom greedy path already audited against native generation

token_target.rule: For each task sample, L2 retains exactly ROI-384 final_context_visual_tokens; if the ROI target exceeds the dense grid, L2 is capped at dense identity and the exception is reported.

protocol.latency_claim: diagnostic within this run only; no formal cross-run latency comparison to ROI-384

interpretation_constraints: The final visual-token and LLM-prefill budgets are matched per sample, except explicitly reported ROI targets larger than dense.
L2 selects after vision layer 5, so six vision blocks still process the dense grid; equal final tokens do not imply equal vision compute.
Oracle ROI reads the ground-truth box and is not deployable.
This experiment identifies representation effects; it does not validate a new controller or establish test-set generalization.
